newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Former PM Wingti concedes defeat in election.
newsitem.headline: Former PM Wingti concedes defeat in election.

text.p: Former Papua New Guinea prime minister Paias Wingti's hopes of becoming prime minister for a third time were dashed on Wednesday when he had to concede defeat in his highlands electorate.
But Wingti vowed he was not finished with national politics.
In the South Pacific nation's fifth general election since independence from Australia in 1975, Wingti lost the Western Highlands regional seat to a local Roman Catholic priest, Father Robert Lak.
"I accept the people's verdict and time will judge if what I have done over the past 20 years is right or wrong," he told reporters.

"In a way I was over confident of retaining the seat of Western Highlands regional because of what I was doing and my past record as minister, prime minister, opposition leader and currently governor of the province," he said.
Wingti was prime minister twice in the late 1980s and early 1990s and had signalled his interest in becoming prime minister again in place of current prime minister and bitter rival, Sir Julius Chan.
He said he would help his People's Democratic Movement (PDM) to form the next government in July, adding that he believed PDM would hold the balance of power in the formation of a government.
Party loyalty is weak in Papua New Guinea and governments are usually decided in post election horse-trading amongst the members of parliament.

Wingti said PDM was ready to work with prime ministerial aspirant Bill Skate, who is governor of the National Capital District, comprising Port Moresby and its environs, and leader of the People's National Congress (PNC),
Seventeen of the 109 seats in the country have been declared so far of which PNC has won two and PDM one.
But Wingti said his party is doing well in the other electorates still polling.
The election started 11 days ago and finishes on Saturday.
Up to three million citizens can vote and the voting takes two weeks to allow voters from remote villages to reach polling stations.
The election results will be officially declared on July 15.
